narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Slightly cooler than yesterday; winds and cloud little changed. Showery from the afternoon, with thunder possible from the morning, peaking this evening. 28°C / 83°F high, 19°C / 66°F low. Sky mostly cloudy early, partly cloudy at midday and overcast in the evening. Wind NE early and WSW at midday; gusts to 46 km/h (25 kt). UV index 9.4 (very high). Air quality 36 (good) at Ochieng' Avenue, Kisumu Central, the highest of 3 stations.

## Extended Outlook

The next three days: warming through Thursday, with rain possible from Wednesday and thunderstorms likely each day. Tuesday will be mostly cloudy with three of four models wet, rain of 0.2–2.1 mm, a high of 30–32 °C, and thunder likely. Wednesday will be partly cloudy with three of four models wet, rain of 0.0–19.9 mm, a high of 31–33 °C, and thunder likely. Thursday, Day+3, will be mostly cloudy with three of four models wet, rain of 0.4–13.4 mm, a high of 29–34 °C, and thunder likely. The Day+3 call is rain at 76%, and Day+7 is rain at 100%. The best rain record for Thursday is ECMWF at 77% of the last 30 checks, and for Monday it is ECMWF at 80%.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Peak CAPE today reaches 3040 J/kg from the UKMO model, with ECMWF at 1790 J/kg, Best Match at 2730 J/kg, and ICON at 1030 J/kg, all above the thunderstorm threshold and peaking at 17:00. Thunder today brings the hazard of sudden gusts well above the forecast wind. No warning is carried in the met service's bulletin.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

The wind timeline for Winam Gulf is overnight at 7 km/h (4 kt) gusting 11 km/h (6 kt), then southwesterly by midday at 10 km/h (6 kt) gusting 21 km/h (11 kt), then north-northwesterly into the evening at 12 km/h (7 kt) gusting 19 km/h (10 kt). The peak gust is 31 km/h (17 kt). Where thunder is possible, the thunderstorm gust hazard is sudden gusts well above the forecast wind.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1010 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1016 hPa), a 6 hPa spread representing a moderate large-scale gradient. Pressure is also falling toward the southwest and west, a large-scale feature building in that direction, though this sampling cannot say how fast or whether it will reach here. Pressure overhead is falling. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Across five points, today's mean sea-level pressure sits between 1014.5 and 1016.3 hPa, falling by 2.5 hPa over three days. The pressure trend is +1.4 hPa, with a moderate large-scale gradient and lowest pressure toward the north.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

At Day+0, no model is meaningfully better than the others yet, based on 46 checks. The call's high of 28°C sits between ECMWF's 27.4°C and GFS's 31°C, with GFS systematically over-forecasting daytime highs and ECMWF slightly under-forecasting them. ECMWF holds the best rain record at Day+0, right 83% of the last 30 checks, yet it systematically under-forecasts peak wind here, sitting on the wrong side of its own record with a gust of 27.4 km/h against the call's 46 km/h. Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) forecasts a high of 28°C and a low of 18°C, agreeing closely with the call's 28°C and 19°C. Data sufficiency is high, with 61 days of stored forecasts reviewed, though coverage for KMD is uneven and lower than the other models.

extended_outlook:
Warming and becoming calmer through Thursday, with showers and thunderstorms likely each day. Skies mostly cloudy Tuesday, then partly cloudy Wednesday and mostly cloudy Thursday. Thursday's call: rain, 76%, with three of four models wet; highs 29 to 34 °C. At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 77% of the time over 58 checks.

Further out, cooling through Monday, with rain and thunderstorms likely Friday, Saturday and Sunday, and rain and thunderstorms possible Monday. Friday: all four models wet, highs 28 to 30 °C. Saturday: all four models wet, the week's wettest day at 17 mm on average, highs 26 to 30 °C. Sunday: all three models that reach it wet, highs 25 to 30 °C.

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Saturday. GFS is the wetter solution from Friday to Saturday; ECMWF, ICON and UKMO keep it drier. Monday's call: rain, 100%, with both models wet; highs 25 to 28 °C. At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 80% of the time over 54 checks.
